title: Emulator, simulator and real device: when each one lies

videos.script: Every test in this half of the course runs on something that is not quite a phone. {{not-a-phone}} An emulator runs real Android on a computer that pretends to be a phone. The iOS simulator does not pretend at all. It runs the app as a program on the Mac. {{two}} And a real phone is the truth, but only for one model, one version and one owner's settings. {{device}} Each of the three hides something. A list that scrolls smoothly on your laptop stutters on a cheap phone. A reminder that fires every time on the emulator never fires on some brands. {{hides}} So this lesson goes through what each one models, and what it leaves out. {{models}} Then a table of defects against the place each one shows up. {{table}} And last, a plan a small team can afford. Emulators for almost everything, a few real phones chosen on purpose, and lesson 20's cloud for the rest. {{plan}}
